title: Noise-area intraday momentum: 1h close above the time-of-day noise band from the UTC open, VWAP trailing exit
ex_ante_rule: Timeframe 1h, closed bars only; a signal at the close of bar t is filled at the open of bar t+1. Long only, spot, one position, whole allowed balance, same rule on BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT, BNB/USDT. Day = UTC calendar day; slot h (0..23) = the 1h bar opening at h:00 UTC. O_d = open of the slot-0 bar of day d. DEFINITIONS: move_d(h) = abs(close of slot h on day d / O_d - 1). sigma_d(h) = arithmetic mean of move_k(h) over the 14 previous completed UTC days k = d-1..d-14 (same slot only; i.e. the 14 bars at offsets 24, 48, ..., 336 back from the current bar; the current day is never included). Upper band U_d(h) = O_d * (1 + sigma_d(h)). Daily VWAP_d(h) = sum(TP*volume) / sum(volume) over the bars of day d from slot 0 through slot h inclusive, TP = (high + low + close)/3; it resets at every slot-0 bar. ENTRY: at the close of a bar in slots 1..19 inclusive (slots 0 and 20..23 never enter) when ALL hold: close > U_d(h); close > VWAP_d(h); no position is open; no trade has been entered yet on this UTC day (counting entry fills; at most one entry per pair per UTC day, also after a stop-out). EXIT (evaluated at the close of every bar while in position, starting with the bar in which the entry was filled): if close < max(U_d(h), VWAP_d(h)) of that bar's slot h, exit at the next open. TIME EXIT: if still in position at the close of the slot-23 bar, exit at the open of the next slot-0 bar (00:00 UTC), so every position lasts at most 23 hours. STOP-LOSS: fixed 3% below the entry price, native intrabar stop (triggers as soon as price touches it). No take-profit, no pyramiding, no cooldown beyond the one-entry-per-day rule, no other filters. If fewer than 14 previous complete days exist, sigma is undefined and no entry is taken. Warm-up: 360 bars (336-bar same-slot lookback plus up to 24 bars of the current day).
rationale: Zarattini, Aziz and Barbon define a noise area as the average absolute move away from the day's open at each time of day over the previous 14 days. Inside it, buy and sell flow is balanced and moves mean-revert. A close outside it means an unusual order-flow imbalance, and that imbalance tends to persist for the rest of the session. The counterparties are large orders executed in slices over the day (rebalancing, hedging) and, in crypto, forced flows: perp short liquidations and buy-stop orders clustered just beyond the usual daily range. All of them buy regardless of price once the range breaks. Requiring close > VWAP means the day's average buyer is in profit, so the break is not a spike against the day's flow. The exit trails at max(band, VWAP): the trade is closed as soon as price falls back into the noise area or below the day's average price, and losing days stay small. I found no published crypto test of this rule; the sources are the SPY paper and write-ups of it. Expected frequency: an upside break of the time-of-day band that is also above VWAP happens on roughly 35-50% of UTC days, so about 130-180 trades per pair per year, within the owner's target. Move per trade: entry needs price already more than one average daily move above the open (in these pairs the mean move by mid-day is about 1-2%). Trend days that continue typically add another 1-3% before the trailing exit, against a round trip of 0.30% (base) or 0.45% (conservative). Losers are cut at the band or VWAP, usually within 0.5-1.5%, with a 3% catastrophic stop. The payoff is skewed: low hit rate, larger winners. Drawdown control comes from the flat-by-00:00 rule (no overnight bear-market exposure), the trailing exit, at most one trade a day, and the 3% stop. Success criteria are the existing gates: positive net at base and conservative cost, drawdown below 25% at optimistic, base and conservative cost, and at least 30 trades per split on all three pairs.
novelty_vs_tried: No tried family uses a time-of-day volatility band anchored at the daily open. The breakout families (Donchian, WeeklyBreakoutRegime, VolatilitySqueezeBreakout, SessionOpeningRangeBreakout, HourlyRangeExpansionDrift, HourlyWilliamsVolBreakout) break a price high/low or an opening range, or scale by ATR. Here the threshold is the slot-specific average distance from the UTC open, so it adapts to the intraday volatility profile (e.g. the US-session hours). WeeklyAnchoredVWAPReclaim used a weekly VWAP as a dip-reclaim entry. Here a daily VWAP is a confirmation and a trailing exit, together with the band, in a momentum trade that is always flat by 00:00 UTC and enters at most once per day.
